name: Stay in the Game
sources: Own calculation: future value of US$50/month at an assumed 8% a year, compounded monthly (FV = 50 × ((1+r)^n − 1)/r, r = 0.08/12).

segments.headline: MOST PEOPLE QUIT
segments.sub: right before it starts to work
segments.say: Most people quit investing right before it starts to work. Here's why.

segments.note: Illustration: US$50/month, assumed 8% average yearly return, compounded monthly. Not guaranteed.
segments.say: Say you put away 50 US dollars a month, and earn an average 8 percent a year. After one year, you'd have about 622 dollars. After five years, about 3,674. It barely feels like anything is happening.

segments.note: Illustration: US$50/month, assumed 8% average yearly return, compounded monthly. Not guaranteed.
segments.say: Five years of effort, and only 674 dollars of that is growth. That's exactly where most people give up.

segments.label: COMPOUNDING
segments.sub: returns that earn their own returns
segments.note: Illustration: US$50/month, assumed 8% average yearly return, compounded monthly. Not guaranteed.
segments.say: But your returns start earning returns of their own. That's compounding, and it speeds up the longer you stay in.

segments.title: AFTER 20 YEARS
segments.note: Illustration: US$50/month, assumed 8% average yearly return, compounded monthly. Not guaranteed.
segments.say: After twenty years, your deposits add up to 12,000 dollars. The account could be worth around 29,000.

segments.title: AFTER 30 YEARS
segments.note: Illustration: US$50/month, assumed 8% average yearly return, compounded monthly. Not guaranteed.
segments.say: After thirty years, 18,000 dollars of deposits could become about 74,000.

segments.note: Illustration: US$50/month, assumed 8% average yearly return, compounded monthly. Not guaranteed.
segments.say: Look at the line. It's flat for years, then it bends upward. About sixty percent of the final balance arrives in the last ten years.

segments.title: THE LESSON
segments.disclaimer: Financial education, not personal advice. Returns are not guaranteed; markets can fall.
segments.say: Start small, stay consistent, be patient. Returns are never guaranteed, and markets fall too. This is financial education, not personal advice. Follow for more.
